camping/canterbury: Canterbury has 22 DOC campsites, and this is a network you can drive to. Campervan access is listed for 18 of them, and Temple Campsite and Mistletoe Flats Campsite list car access only. Loch Katrine Campsite in Lake Sumner Forest Park has no access mode recorded, and Orari Campsite in the Geraldine area is marked closed, so check both before you plan a night there.

Paid sites charge adults $10 to $23 a night, and $10 is the usual figure: Wooded Gully Campsite in Mount Thomas Forest Conservation Area, Waihī Gorge, Otaio Gorge, Mt Nimrod and Lake Middleton all ask $10. The 6 free campsites are all basic ones with non-flush toilets, including Ahuriri Bridge Campsite near Omarama, Quailburn Campsite in Ahuriri Conservation Park, and Temple and Round Bush campsites in Ruataniwha Conservation Park. Of the 22, 14 can be booked online through DOC; the rest are first come.

Arthur's Pass National Park holds 4 campsites, ranging from free to $18. Andrews Shelter Campsite is free, Hawdon Shelter costs $10, Klondyke Corner $15 and Avalanche Creek Shelter $18. Avalanche Creek Shelter is the only campsite in the region that lists treated tap water, and it also has flush toilets and a cooking shelter. Lake Sumner Forest Park adds Lake Taylor and Boyle at $10 each, and Craigieburn Forest Park has Lake Pearson (Moana Rua) and Mistletoe Flats at $15.

Peel Forest Campground, in Peel Forest Park Scenic Reserve, is the outlier. It is the region's only serviced campsite and its largest, with 81 sites, and the only one with powered sites or hot showers; adults pay $20 to $23. Elsewhere, plan on non-flush toilets at most sites (flush toilets are listed at 5) and untreated tap or stream water, so carry a way to treat it. Campfires are permitted at 6 campsites, subject to fire season rules, and 8 allow dogs in some form. The region also has 180 DOC huts for trips further in.
camping/central-north-island: Most DOC camping in the Central North Island costs nothing. Of the 14 campsites, 9 are free, and every free one is a basic campsite. Kaimanawa Forest Park accounts for 7 of them: Clements Clearing, Waikoko, Kaimanawa Road, Urchin, Army Road, Kakapo and Te Iringa campsites are all free, all open to campervans, and all allow campfires (fire season rules apply). Facilities there are simple: non-flush toilets and, at most, stream water.

Tongariro National Park holds 5 campsites, and they are the paid ones. Mangahuia and Mangawhero are standard campsites reached by road at $18 a night for adults, with untreated tap water. The other three are Great Walk campsites, Mangatepopo, Oturere and Waihohonu, reached only on foot. Their adult rate is $10 to $19 for NZ residents and $10 to $28 for international visitors, which is where the top of the region's $10 to $28 range comes from.

The largest campsite by number of sites is Pokaka Mill Campsite, with 30, in Tongariro Forest Conservation Area. It is free, but its only listed access is 4WD, so a campervan or ordinary car is not the vehicle for it. Near Taupō, Whakaipo Campsite is free and open to self-contained campervans only.

Before you go, note what no campsite in the region lists: no flush toilets, no showers, no treated tap water and no powered sites. Bring your own water treatment and expect to be self-sufficient. In return, 9 campsites allow dogs in some form and 7 permit campfires. Only 5 of the 14 are bookable online through DOC, so most nights here are first come. The landscape mix is forest, alpine and rivers and lakes, and there are 16 DOC huts in the region for those heading further in.
camping/coromandel: Free DOC camping is almost absent from the Coromandel. Of its 20 campsites, 18 charge a fee and 19 can be booked online through DOC, so plan ahead rather than counting on a spare pitch. The one free campsite is Moss Creek Campsite in Coromandel Forest Park, a backcountry site reached on foot with non-flush toilets and nothing else listed.

Coromandel Forest Park holds 14 campsites. Many are roadside standard sites at $10 a night for adults, with non-flush toilets and stream water: Booms Flat, Catleys, Totara Flat, Wainora, Hotoritori and Shag Stream all fit that pattern. Whangaiterenga Campsite is also $10 and is the only campsite in the region with flush toilets. Kahikatea Campsite is for self-contained campervans only, at $13, and has powered sites. Further in, Trestle View ($10), Billygoat Basin ($10), Dancing Camp ($12.50) and Crosbies Hut Backcountry Campsite ($12.50 to $15) are all reached on foot.

Northern Coromandel is the coastal end, with 5 campsites, and every one has cold showers. Waikawau Bay Campsite is the region's largest, with 132 sites, powered sites and an adult rate of $18 to $23. Port Jackson costs $18 to $20, while Stony Bay, Fletcher Bay and Fantail Bay are $18 each. All of them take campervans, though Port Jackson, Fletcher Bay and Fantail Bay are classed as backcountry campsites.

Across the region, 14 campsites list campervan access and the landscape runs from forest to rivers and lakes to coast. Where water is listed, it is untreated tap or stream water, so carry a filter or boil it. Only 2 campsites allow dogs in some form. Wentworth Valley Campground appears in the list without fee, access or facility details, so check DOC before relying on it. With just 2 DOC huts in the region, campsites far outnumber huts here.
camping/east-coast: DOC camping on the East Coast is cheap or free. Of 14 campsites, 8 are free, and the adult rates that are listed run from $8 to $15 a night. Mokau Landing Campsite in Te Urewera, at $8, is the cheapest paid site and has a boat ramp. Only 3 campsites are bookable online through DOC, so most of the network works on first come.

Te Urewera holds 6 of the campsites. Te Pakau (Eight Acre) and Omahuru (Ogilvies) charge $10, while Orangihikoia, Te Taita A Makoro and Rosie Bay are free basic campsites open to campervans. Omahuru has flush toilets; the others have non-flush toilets. In the Lake Waikaremoana area, Waikaremoana Holiday Park is the region's only serviced campsite, with powered sites, hot showers and flush toilets. Its fee is not listed, only noted as applying.

Whirinaki Te Pua-a-Tāne Conservation Park has 3 free campsites. Mid Okahu Road and Sanctuary campsites take campervans, and Verns Camp is reached only on foot, the one campsite in the region with no vehicle access. In the Ōpōtiki area, Manganuku Campsite costs $10 and has flush toilets, while Boulders and Whitikau are free; Boulders lists car access only and has a barbecue.

Campfires are permitted at 9 campsites, with fire season rules applying. Showers and powered sites are found only at the holiday park, and none of the listed campsites has treated tap water, so bring a way to treat what you collect. Dogs are allowed in some form at 4. The largest campsite by sites, Anaura Bay Campsite with 81, is marked closed in the data. The landscape is mostly rivers and lakes and forest, and the region also has 38 DOC huts.
camping/fiordland: Every one of Fiordland's 13 DOC campsites sits in Fiordland National Park, and they fall into three clear groups: roadside standard campsites, Great Walk campsites, and free basic sites by the water.

The roadside group is the simplest to plan. Cascade Creek, Henry Creek, Totara, Deer Flat, Kiosk Creek, Walker Creek and Upper Eglinton are standard campsites at a flat $18 a night for adults. Cascade Creek Campsite is the largest in the region, with 120 sites, a cooking shelter and wheelchair access. Walker Creek and Upper Eglinton list campervan and car access but not caravans. Facilities are basic across the group: non-flush toilets and stream water at most.

Brod Bay, Iris Burn and Lake Mackenzie are Great Walk campsites, reached only on foot. The adult rate is $10 to $28 for NZ residents and $10 to $42 for international visitors, the top of the region's $10 to $42 range. Each has a cooking shelter, non-flush toilets and untreated tap water.

The 3 free campsites are all basic. Hall Arm Campsite is reached only by boat. South Arm Campsite (Lake Manapouri) lists boat and car access, and Monowai Campsite takes campervans and has a boat ramp. Together with the Great Walk sites, that makes 4 campsites with no road access.

Some things are missing across the whole region: none of the 13 lists flush toilets, showers, treated tap water or powered sites, and none allows dogs. Carry water treatment and plan to be self-sufficient. Campfires are permitted at 7 campsites under fire season rules, mostly among the roadside group. Of the 13, 10 can be booked online through DOC. The landscape is rivers and lakes and forest, and the region has 55 DOC huts for multi-day trips.
camping/manawatu-whanganui: DOC camping in Manawatū/Whanganui is largely river camping. Whanganui National Park holds 16 of the region's 20 campsites, and 11 campsites are Great Walk campsites. Only 3 campsites list campervan access, so most of this network is reached on the water, on foot or by mountain bike.

The Great Walk campsites along the river, among them Ngaporo, Tīeke Marae/Kāinga, John Coull, Mangawaiiti, Ohauora, Mangapapa, Maharanui, Poukaria and Mangapurua, are reached only by boat. The adult rate is $12 to $19 a night, and each has a cooking shelter, non-flush toilets and untreated tap water. Ohinepane Campsite, the largest with 36 sites, and Whakahoro Campsite are different: both take campervans and caravans, have boat ramps and wheelchair access, and charge $10 to $19.

Away from the river, the backcountry campsites are walking and biking stops. Atene Skyline Campsite is reached on foot; Hellawell's, Johnsons, Mosley's, Bettjemann and Mangapurua Trig list foot and mountain bike access. Mosley's and Bettjemann are the 2 free campsites in the region, and several others show no fee in the data, so confirm the charge with DOC. Facilities are mostly limited to a non-flush toilet, so carry water.

Pohangina Base Campsite in the Pohangina Valley area is the region's one standard campsite. At $12 a night for adults it has hot showers and flush toilets, the only ones in the region. Piripiri Campsite, also in the Pohangina Valley area, is listed with no details, and Simpsons Domain Campsite near Hunterville is marked closed.

Of the 20, 12 can be booked online through DOC. Dogs are allowed in some form at 2. No campsite in the region lists powered sites or treated tap water, so bring water treatment for the whole trip. There are 43 DOC huts in the region as well.
camping/marlborough: Marlborough has 44 DOC campsites, and the landscape count says it plainly: 37 are coastal. The Pelorus Sound/Te Hoiere and Kenepuru Sound area holds 15, the Queen Charlotte Sound/Tōtaranui area 11, and the French Pass and D'Urville Island Scenic Reserves 6. With 25 campsites reached only on foot or by boat and only 15 with campervan access, sort out how you will get there before you choose a campsite.

The boat-access sites are cheap. Ratimera Bay, Wharehunga Bay, Jacobs Bay, Ferndale and Blumine Island/Oruawairua campsites are reached by boat at $10 a night for adults, with non-flush toilets and untreated tap water. Black Rock, Nydia and Schoolhouse Bay are $10 too and can be reached on foot or by mountain bike. South Arm Campsite in the French Pass and D'Urville Island Scenic Reserves is free and boat only.

If you are driving, look at the Blenheim area and Marfells Beach. Whites Bay Campsite is the largest, with 67 sites, at $15, with flush toilets and cold showers. Rarangi and Marfells Beach are also $15 with flush toilets and cold showers. Pelorus Bridge Campground is the only serviced campsite, at $25 to $27, with powered sites, hot showers and treated tap water, which is the top of the region's $10 to $27 range.

Inland, Molesworth Recreation Reserve offers Acheron Accommodation House and Molesworth Cob Cottage at $10 and Lake Tennyson for free. Mount Richmond Forest Park has Onamalutu ($10, with powered sites), Butchers Flat ($10) and Mill Flat, which is free but 4WD only.

Across the region, 10 campsites are free and 33 charge a fee, and 20 can be booked online through DOC. Dogs are allowed in some form at 12. Treated tap water is listed at only 2 campsites, so plan to treat water elsewhere. The data marks 6 campsites closed, so check the one you want before you go. There are also 60 DOC huts.
camping/nelson-tasman: Great Walk campsites dominate Nelson/Tasman. Of the region's 37 DOC campsites, 25 are Great Walk campsites, and 26 are reached only on foot or by boat. Abel Tasman National Park alone holds 17. Just 8 list campervan access, and 31 can be booked online through DOC, so this is a region for booking ahead.

In Abel Tasman National Park, the Great Walk campsites charge adults $21 a night as NZ residents and $21 to $31 as international visitors, the top of the region's $10 to $31 range. Bark Bay, Onetahuti Bay, Mutton Cove, Anapai Bay, Waiharakeke Bay and Whariwharangi Bay have flush toilets; Apple Tree Bay, Tinline, Te Pukatea Bay and Torrent Bay Village have non-flush toilets. Mosquito Bay is listed as boat access only. Tōtaranui Campground is the exception: a standard campsite with 269 sites, the largest in the region, reached by campervan or boat, with cold showers, treated tap water and a dump station, at $18 to $20.

Kahurangi National Park holds 9 campsites. The Great Walk sites listed there, Heaphy, Brown and Scotts Beach, are $19 for NZ residents and $19 to $28 for international visitors. Heaphy and Brown also list mountain bike access and have flush toilets.

Nelson Lakes National Park has 6 campsites and most of the region's campervan access. Kerr Bay Campsite is the only serviced campsite, at $25 to $30, with powered sites, hot showers, flush toilets and treated tap water. The two West Bay zones, Buller and Jetty, are $20 with cold showers and treated tap water. Teetotal and Lake Rotoroa campsites cost $15, and Lake Rotoroa has a boat ramp and jetty.

Free camping is scarce: only 2 campsites are free, including Cobb River Campsite in the Cobb Valley, reached by 4WD or car. Dogs are allowed in some form at just 2. Campfires are permitted at 8 under fire season rules. The region also has 99 DOC huts.
camping/northland: Northland's DOC campsites are mostly coastal, and showers are the norm rather than the exception. Of the 14 campsites, 12 are coastal and 11 have showers, mostly cold. Uretiti Beach Campsite in the Waipū area is the largest, with 300 sites, hot showers and treated tap water, the only campsite in the region that lists it, at $18 a night for adults.

Rates run from $10 to $23. Most standard campsites sit at $18 or $20: Maitai Bay on the Karikari Peninsula and Rarawa Beach are $18, Otamure Bay (Whananaki) and Puriri Bay (Whangaruru North Head) are $20, and both of these last two have a boat ramp. Trounson Kauri Park Campground, the only serviced campsite, charges $20 to $23 and has powered sites, hot showers and flush toilets. At the low end, Puketī Recreation Area Campsite costs $10 and is the one campsite in the region where campfires are permitted, under fire season rules.

Urupukapuka Island Recreation Reserve has 3 campsites, Urupukapuka Bay, Cable Bay and Sunset Bay, and all are reached only by boat, at $18 to $20. In the far north, Cape Reinga/Te Rerenga Wairua has Kapowairua (Spirits Bay) and Tapotupotu, both $18 with campervan, car or foot access and cold showers.

The 2 free campsites are quite different. Raetea North Side Campsite is a basic roadside site with non-flush toilets and stream water. Twilight Campsite in Te Paki Recreation Reserve is a backcountry campsite reached only on foot, with a cooking shelter and untreated tap water.

None of Northland's campsites lists dogs as allowed, so leave them at home for DOC nights. Of the 14, 11 can be booked online through DOC and 10 take campervans. With only 7 DOC huts in the region, campsites outnumber huts here 14 to 7.
camping/otago: Otago's 30 DOC campsites cover a wide price spread, from $5 to $42 a night for adults. The cheap end is the backcountry. Aspiring Campsite in the Matukituki Valley area is $5, with a non-flush toilet. Campsites at huts cost $10: Dart Campsite (near hut) and Shelter Rock in Mount Aspiring National Park, and Greenstone, McKellar and Mid Caples in the Greenstone and Caples Conservation Areas. All of these are reached on foot, and the hut campsites list flush toilets.

The top of the range is Routeburn Flats Campsite, the region's one Great Walk campsite, at $10 to $28 for NZ residents and $10 to $42 for international visitors. Mount Aspiring National Park holds the most campsites, with 6, and also has Pleasant Flat Campsite, a roadside standard site at $15 with flush toilets and a cooking shelter.

For campervans, 17 campsites list access. Around Queenstown and Glenorchy, Twelve Mile Delta Campsite is the largest, with 100 sites, at $18, with a boat ramp; Moke Lake, Sylvan and Kinloch are also $18, and Kinloch has a jetty. Kidds Bush Reserve Campsite in Hāwea Conservation Park and Cameron Flat in the Makarora area cost $15. Skippers Campsite is $10 but lists only 4WD and mountain bike access.

Of the 8 free campsites, Homestead Campsite in Oteake Conservation Park, Lindis Pass Historic Hotel Campsite and St Bathans Domain Campsite can be reached by campervan. Macetown Campsite is free but needs a 4WD, a bike or your feet, and Beach Point at Walter Peak Campsite is reached on foot, by boat or by mountain bike.

Dogs are allowed in some form at 12 campsites. Campfires are permitted at only 2, Tawanui and Purakaunui Bay in the Catlins coastal area. No campsite lists showers, powered sites or treated tap water. Of the 30, 16 are bookable online through DOC and 2 are marked closed. The region also has 78 DOC huts.
camping/west-coast: West Coast DOC campsites are spread thinly along the region rather than clustered in one park; no single area holds more than 2. Of the 14, 13 charge a fee, between $10 and $20 a night for adults, and 12 can be booked online through DOC. Most are standard campsites that a campervan can reach: 10 list campervan access.

Lake campsites stand out. Lake Māhinapua Campsite is the largest, with 100 sites, at $18, with flush toilets, cold showers and a boat ramp; it is the only campsite in the region with showers. Hans Bay – Lake Kaniere Campsite costs $15 and has a boat ramp and jetty. Lake Ianthe Matahi Campsite in the Harihari area is $10 with a boat ramp, and Lake Paringa Campsite is $18.

Several campsites have barbecues: Kōhaihai in Kahurangi National Park ($10), Marble Hill in Lewis Pass Scenic Reserve ($15), Lyell ($18) and Slab Hut Creek in Victoria Forest Park ($15). Goldsborough Campsite is another $10 option, with flush toilets. Otto/MacDonalds Campsite, listed under Franz Josef Glacier, is $18 with flush toilets. Gillespies Beach Campsite costs $18 to $20 and lists car access only, not campervan access.

The 3 campsites with no road access need walking boots. Ballroom Overhang Campsite in Paparoa National Park is the only free campsite in the region and is reached on foot, with a non-flush toilet. Lake Daniell Campsite in Lewis Pass Scenic Reserve ($10) and Welcome Flat Campsite in Westland Tai Poutini National Park ($15) are backcountry campsites with untreated tap water.

Flush toilets are listed at 5 campsites. No campsite lists treated tap water or powered sites, so carry water treatment. Dogs are allowed in some form at 4. With 140 DOC huts in the region, there are also plenty of roofed options for longer trips.
freedom-camping/central-otago: DOC's Central Otago district has 13 current freedom camping notices on public conservation land, and 11 of them prohibit freedom camping outright. Only 2 areas are restricted rather than closed. These notices were made by DOC for land it manages. They are not council bylaws, and they do not cover reserves, roadsides or car parks run by a council. All the listed areas lie in Queenstown Lakes District, around Wanaka, Albert Town, Luggate, Makarora and the Crown Range, so wherever you are on council land rather than conservation land, the Queenstown Lakes District Council freedom camping rules apply instead.

Most of the prohibited land sits in just two notices. Newcastle Track is the largest notice area at 81.8 ha, and Deans Bank, Dublin Bay tracks covers 51.4 ha, which together account for most of the 143.4 ha where camping is prohibited. The rest are small: Roys Peak Track carpark (0.3 ha), Diamond Lake, Wanaka (0.3 ha), Cameron Flat River Access (0.6 ha), Albert Town Outlet carpark (1.2 ha) and the Mt Aspiring National Park Visitor Centre, Wanaka (0.4 ha) among them. Prohibited means no freedom camping in that area at all, whether or not your vehicle is certified self-contained.

The 2 restricted areas, 1.2 ha between them, carry quite different conditions, so read each one on its own. At Crown Range Summit you may freedom camp only in a certified self-contained vehicle, and for no more than 4 nights in a calendar month. At Raspberry Creek carpark the notice sets a time window instead: camping is allowed only between 5 pm and 9 am, so arrive in the evening and be gone by morning.

The current notices come from two dates. Of them, 7 were made on 1 December 2012 and 6 on 1 December 2017, with notice numbers running from 119 to 290, and together they sit on 10 distinct conservation land parcels. A further 2 notices for this district are historic and no longer current, so if an older list names a spot that is missing here, check it against the current notices before relying on it.
freedom-camping/hawkes-bay: Restricted areas in the Hawkes Bay district all follow one pattern. Of 16 current DOC notices, 6 restrict freedom camping and every one of those 6 carries the same pair of conditions: self-contained vehicles only, and no more than 4 nights in a calendar month. The other 10 prohibit it.

The restricted areas are Balls Clearing Roadend Carpark, Elsthorpe Carpark, Mohi Bush Picnic Area, Shine Falls Roadend Amenity Area, Tangoio Falls and White Pine Bush Picnic Area. In practice you need a certified self-contained vehicle to stay at any of them, and a tent or an uncertified van is not allowed. Mohi Bush Picnic Area is the biggest at 4 ha of the 5.9 ha that is restricted.

Prohibited areas cover 21.2 ha. Cape Kidnappers Track Amenity Area is the largest single notice area at 11.4 ha. The list also takes in Kuripapango Amenity Area (3 ha), Lake Tutira Amenity Area, Lake Tutira Boat Ramp Amenity Area, Opouahi Scenic Reserve, Pohokura Roadend Carpark, Lotkow Amenity Area and two urban sites: Humber Street, Ahuriri Estuary, Napier and Otatara Pa, Taradale. No freedom camping is allowed at any of these.

Nearly the whole set dates from 1 December 2012, when 15 of the current notices were made. The exception is Monckton Carpark, prohibited by notice 297 on 13 November 2021. Notice numbers run from 23 to 297, the notices cover 27.1 ha on 14 distinct conservation land parcels, and 3 older notices for the district are historic and no longer current.

Keep in mind that these are DOC notices for conservation land, not council bylaws. Council reserves, roadsides and car parks are covered by the council's own freedom camping rules instead: the Napier City Council freedom camping rules around Napier and Taradale, the Hastings District Council freedom camping rules in Hastings District, where most of the listed areas lie, and the Central Hawke's Bay District Council freedom camping rules further south around Elsthorpe.
freedom-camping/new-plymouth: The New Plymouth district has 22 current DOC freedom camping notices: 13 prohibit camping and 9 restrict it. All 9 restricted areas share the core conditions of self-contained vehicles only and no more than 4 nights in a calendar month, so a certified self-contained vehicle is the minimum for staying overnight at any of them.

At Everett Park Carparks and Mangaoraka Carpark the notices go further. Camping there is allowed only between 5 pm and 9 am, and the notices record that the restrictions apply 1 November to 30 April. The other restricted areas are Dawson Falls Carparks, North Egmont Carparks, Potaema Carpark, Puniho Carpark, Stratford Mountain House Carparks, Stratford Plateau Carparks and Upper Lucys Gully Carpark.

Look closely at the names, because several sites have a prohibited notice area and a restricted one under almost the same name. Dawson Falls view carpark is prohibited while Dawson Falls Carparks is restricted, and the same split applies to Potaema Amenity Area and Potaema Carpark, to Upper Lucys Gully Amenity Area and Upper Lucys Gully Carpark, and to Stratford Mtn House Amenity Area and Stratford Mountain House Carparks. Lower North Egmont Amenity Area is prohibited, North Egmont Carparks restricted.

Prohibited areas total 30.7 ha and restricted areas 15.5 ha, 46.2 ha in all across 6 distinct conservation land parcels. The largest notice area is Pukerangiora Pa Carpark at 14.8 ha, followed by Gordon Block at 7.4 ha, and both are prohibited. Nearly every notice dates from 1 December 2012 (20 of them); Gordon Block and Dawson Falls view carpark were added on 1 December 2017. Notice numbers run from 165 to 289, and 1 earlier notice is now historic.

None of this is a council bylaw. DOC's notices cover only public conservation land. On land the council controls, the New Plymouth District Council freedom camping rules apply, and Ohura Peak Amenity Area lies in Ruapehu District, where the Ruapehu District Council freedom camping rules cover council land. Several listed areas fall in neighbouring districts, so check whose land you are on before you stop for the night.
freedom-camping/south-westland: DOC's South Westland district has 18 current freedom camping notices on public conservation land. Of these, 17 prohibit camping outright and just 1 is restricted. These are DOC notices for land it manages, not council bylaws: on roadsides, reserves and car parks the council controls, the Westland District Council freedom camping rules apply instead.

The one restricted area is Whakapohai Road, South Westland, covering 3.1 ha. You may freedom camp there only in a certified self-contained vehicle, and for no more than 4 nights in a calendar month. Every other area on the list is closed to freedom camping, whatever you are driving and however self-contained it is.

The prohibited areas are mostly small car parks at the places visitors stop: Fox Glacier Visitor Centre Carpark, Franz Josef Glacier Road and Carparks, Lake Matheson Carpark, Haast Visitor Centre Carpark, Knights Point Viewpoint Carparks, Ship Creek Amenity Area and Carpark, Monro Beach Walk Carpark and Westland National Park Visitor Centre. Many cover less than 1 ha, and Wharekai -Te Kou Walk Carparks is the smallest at 0.1 ha. Roaring Billy Walk carpark is the largest notice area at 18.4 ha, ahead of Okarito Recreation Reserve at 9.9 ha, and prohibited land totals 41.9 ha of the 45 ha covered.

Three notices are recent. MacDonalds Creek and Peak Viewpoint were prohibited on 13 November 2021, and Southside Road, Fox Glacier Carparks on 13 December 2021; the other 15 date from 1 December 2012. Notice numbers run from 84 to 304, the notices sit on 12 distinct conservation land parcels, and 1 older notice for the district is historic and no longer current, so check an older list against these before relying on it.
freedom-camping/te-anau: DOC's Te Anau district has 24 current freedom camping notices on public conservation land, and every one of them prohibits camping. There are no restricted areas here, so no notice lets even a certified self-contained vehicle stay: if a place is on this list, you cannot freedom camp there at all. The notices cover 4,046.5 ha in total. They were made by DOC for land it manages and are not council bylaws; on council land around Te Anau, the Southland District Council freedom camping rules apply instead.

One notice dwarfs the rest. Patience Bay, Milford Road is the largest notice area at 2,107.6 ha, more than half of the total. Eweburn covers 609.3 ha, Queens and Rainbow Reaches carparks 370.2 ha and Margin Forest 181.7 ha. At the other end, Pearl Harbour, Waiau River is the smallest at 1.1 ha, and Te Anau AO and Visitor Centre Carparks covers 1.6 ha, so the list runs from large blocks of land down to single car parks in town.

Many of the notices sit along the road to Milford: The Divide Carpark, Lake Gunn Walk Carpark, Lake Marian Falls Track Carpark, Mistake Creek Track Carpark, Monkey Creek, The Chasm Carpark, Hollyford Roadend and Moraine Creek Carpark, Homer Nature Walk & Gertrude Valley Track and Tutuko Valley Track. Of the 24 notices, 12 share one conservation land parcel. Kepler Track and Control Gate Carparks and Te Anau Downs and Lake Mistletoe Carparks are on the list too, so trailhead parking is not a place to sleep.

All 24 current notices were made on the same day in December 2012, with notice numbers running from 230 to 256, and none for this district is historic, so this list is the whole current picture for DOC land here. For somewhere to stay, look at the DOC campsites in the area or the council's rules for its own land, and read the freedom camping rules guide before you set off.
freedom-camping/tongariro: Prohibited areas dominate the Tongariro district. Of 22 current DOC notices, 17 prohibit freedom camping, and the largest notice area, Whakapapa Village at 43.5 ha, is one of them. Ohakune Lakes adds another 16.8 ha, and most of the rest are car parks at track ends, falls and viewpoints: Mangatepopo Roadend Carpark, Ketetahi Road Carpark, Tawhai Falls Carpark, Mounds Walk Carpark, Waitonga Falls Carpark, Raurimu Spiral Viewpoint and the Ohakune Visitor Centre among them. In a prohibited area you cannot freedom camp at all.

Restricted areas number 5, and each one requires a self-contained vehicle and allows no more than 4 nights in a calendar month: Dominion Rd Carpark, Okupata Caves Carpark, Rangataua Road End Carpark, Taurewa Loop Track Carpark and Tukino Mountain Road Carpark. Rangataua Road End Carpark is the biggest at 19.6 ha. Tukino Mountain Road Carpark carries extra conditions as well, with camping allowed only between 5 pm and 9 am and restrictions that apply 1 November to 30 April.

In all, the notices cover 103 ha, 78.4 ha prohibited and 24.6 ha restricted, spread over just 4 distinct conservation land parcels. Notice numbers run from 163 to 227. Most date from 1 December 2012 (20 notices); Scoria Flat Carpark followed in 2015 and Raurimu Spiral Viewpoint in 2017. A single older notice is historic and no longer current.

These notices apply to public conservation land only. They are not council bylaws, and they say nothing about council reserves, roadsides or town car parks. Most of the listed areas are in Ruapehu District and the remainder in Taupō District, and on council land there the Ruapehu District Council freedom camping rules or the Taupō District Council freedom camping rules apply. Being outside a DOC notice area does not by itself mean a spot is open for camping, so check the council's rules for the land you are on.
freedom-camping/turangi: In the Turangi district the restricted land far outweighs the prohibited land, even though prohibited notices are more numerous. Of 28 current DOC notices, 21 prohibit freedom camping and 7 restrict it, yet the restricted areas cover 289.7 ha against 52.3 ha prohibited. Nearly all of that restricted land is one place: Whakaipo Amenity Area, the largest notice area at 281.2 ha.

Whakaipo needs care, because two notices share nearly the same name. Whakaipo Amenity Area (Lakeshore) is a separate 15.7 ha notice where camping is prohibited outright, while the wider Whakaipo Amenity Area is restricted. All 7 restricted areas carry the same conditions, self-contained vehicles only and no more than 4 nights in a calendar month, so you need a certified self-contained vehicle at Whakaipo Amenity Area, Hinemaiaia Reserve Carparks, Huka-Aratiatia Amenity Area, Pillars of Hercules Carpark, Southern Access Corridor, Umukarikari Carpark and Urchin Carpark.

The 21 prohibited areas are mostly small car parks, picnic areas and amenity areas, including Tokaanu Hot Pools Carparks, Major Jones Amenity Area, Stag Pool Carpark, Cliff Pool Carpark, Hatepe Picnic Area, Mission Bay Amenity Area and Taupo Landing and Yacht Club carpark. The bigger ones are Parikarangaranga Picnic Site at 14.4 ha and Awaroa Amenity Area at 10.1 ha. No freedom camping is allowed in any of them.

These notices built up over several years rather than in one round. Of the current notices, 19 date from 2012, 2 from 2014, 3 from 2016, 3 from 2017 and 1 from 2021, when Five Mile Bay Amenity Area was prohibited on 13 November 2021. Notice numbers run from 161 to 296, and the areas sit on 19 distinct conservation land parcels. A further 10 notices are historic and no longer current, so check any older list against the current notices.

All of this applies to public conservation land only. These are DOC notices, not council bylaws, and the reserves, roadsides and car parks run by the council are governed by the Taupō District Council freedom camping rules, so the rules can change as you move from DOC land to council land.
freedom-camping/wakatipu: The road from Queenstown to Glenorchy shapes much of the Wakatipu list. DOC has 29 current freedom camping notices in this district and 21 of them prohibit camping. Most of those prohibited areas are named stops along Queenstown-Glenorchy Road, from Bobs Cove, Twelve Mile Delta and Wilson Bay to Bennetts Bluff, White Point, Rat Point and Lake Face Creek. If you are driving that road, treat each of these as closed to freedom camping.

Away from the lakeside road, prohibited areas include Routeburn Roadend (6.7 ha), Routeburn - Weka Flat, Morning Star Beach, Mt Alfred Carpark, Lake Kirkpatrick, Moke Road (4 ha) and Roaring Meg carpark and picnic area. Oxenbridge Reserve is the largest notice area in the district at 8.6 ha, and it too is prohibited. Prohibited land totals 34.1 ha.

The 8 restricted areas, covering 10.5 ha, are where the conditions matter. Of those 8, 7 are for self-contained vehicles only, 7 allow no more than 4 nights in a calendar month and 6 allow camping only between 5 pm and 9 am. Chinamans Bluff carpark, Diamond Lake, Glenorchy, Glacier Burn Carpark and Greenstone River carpark carry every one of those conditions, so arrive after 5 pm in a certified self-contained vehicle and leave by 9 am. Diamond Lake needs particular care: Diamond Lake, Glenorchy is restricted, but the separate Diamond Lake, Glenorchy - Bloomfields Hill notice is prohibited.

Notice dates are 1 December 2012 for 20 of the current notices and 1 December 2017 for 9, with notice numbers from 121 to 288 across 21 distinct conservation land parcels. This district also has 13 historic notices that are no longer current, so an older list may include notices that no longer apply.

These notices cover public conservation land only and are not council bylaws. On the roadsides, reserves and car parks that the council manages, the Queenstown Lakes District Council freedom camping rules apply regardless of the DOC notices.
huts/canterbury: Canterbury has 180 DOC huts with 1,155 bunks between them, and the bulk of them are simple shelters. Basic huts and bivvies account for 108, standard huts for 47, serviced huts for 16 and serviced alpine huts for 9. Carrington Hut in Arthur's Pass National Park has the most bunks at 36, a serviced hut charging adults $25 a night with heating and mattresses.

Free and paid huts are close to even here: 92 cost nothing and 84 carry a fee. Adult rates in the data run from $10 to $55 a night. The top of that range is Mueller Hut, a serviced alpine hut in Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park with 28 bunks at $55. Plateau Hut in the same park sleeps 33, with a fee but no rate in the data. Woolshed Creek Hut in Hakatere Conservation Park lists $12.50 to $35 for its 26 bunks, while Goat Pass Hut and Crow Hut in Arthur's Pass National Park are standard huts at $10. Just 13 huts must be booked through DOC, so most are first come, first served.

Lake Sumner Forest Park holds the most huts with 26, ahead of Arthur's Pass National Park on 22 and the Rangitata and Rakaia Rivers area on 20. In Lake Sumner Forest Park, Hope Kiwi Lodge is a serviced hut with 20 bunks, and Hurunui Hut sleeps 15 for $10. Anne Hut, Boyle Flat Hut and Christopher Hut in the St James Conservation Area are serviced huts listed at $10 to $25.

Heating is listed at 117 huts and mattresses at 140, so not every hut has them. Water comes from a stream at 108 huts, which means carrying a way to treat or boil it. Only 14 huts are listed as within 3 hours of a road, and 5 are marked closed in the data, so check a hut's status before you walk in. DOC also runs 22 campsites in the region, covered on their own page.
huts/central-north-island: Only one of the 16 DOC huts in the Central North Island is free: Ten Man Hut, a basic hut with 8 bunks in the Tongariro Forest Conservation Area. The other 15 charge a fee. Together the huts hold 228 bunks, and the categories are spread fairly evenly, with 6 serviced huts, 5 standard huts, 3 Great Walk huts and 2 basic huts or bivvies.

Tongariro National Park holds 10 of the huts, including all 3 Great Walk huts. Waihohonu Hut has the most bunks in the region at 28, followed by Oturere Hut with 26 and Mangatepopo Hut with 20. Their adult rates are split by residency: $25 to $44 a night for NZ residents and $25 to $66 for international visitors, which is where the region's top rate of $66 comes from. The serviced huts in the park, among them Rangipo Hut, Blyth Hut, Mangaehuehu Hut and Whakapapaiti Hut, charge adults $25, and Lupton Hut is a standard hut with 8 bunks at $15.

Kaimanawa Forest Park has 4 huts. Boyd Hut is the serviced one, with 16 bunks at $25. Oamaru Hut and Waipakihi Hut are standard huts with 12 bunks each at $10, and Cascade Hut sleeps 6 at the same rate. Zekes Hut is the single hut in Hihitahi Forest Sanctuary, a standard hut with 4 bunks at $10.

Facilities are consistent across the region. Heating is listed at 15 of the 16 huts and mattresses at all 16. DOC requires bookings at 5 huts, and 4 are listed as within 3 hours of a road. Adult rates across the paid huts run from $10 to $66. If a hut night is not what you need, DOC runs 14 campsites in the region as well.
huts/east-coast: Of the 38 DOC huts on the East Coast, 11 are marked closed in the data, so a hut's current status is the first thing to confirm. Between them the 38 huts hold 403 bunks, and every one of them lists both heating and mattresses. Standard huts dominate with 28, alongside 5 basic huts or bivvies, 4 Great Walk huts and a single serviced hut.

Te Urewera holds 16 huts, including all 4 Great Walk huts and the region's largest. Waiharuru Hut has 40 bunks, Panekire Hut 36, Waiopaoa Hut 30 and Marauiti Hut 26. The data shows a fee for each of them but no rate, so the listed adult range of $10 to $25 does not cover them. Sandy Bay Hut, also in Te Urewera, is the one serviced hut, with 18 bunks and no fee listed.

Whirinaki Te Pua-a-Tāne Conservation Park has 10 huts, almost all standard huts at $10 a night. Central Whirinaki Hut is the biggest there with 25 bunks and a $10 to $25 rate, Central Te Hoe Hut sleeps 15, and Mangamate Hut, Moerangi Hut and Upper Whirinaki Hut have 9 bunks each.

Only 4 huts are free. Manganuku Hut in the Ōpōtiki area is one, a basic hut with 6 bunks and water from a stream; Mangakirikiri Hut in Raukumara Conservation Park is another. The rest of the Ōpōtiki area's 5 huts include Kotepato Hut, Nikau Flat Hut and Pakihi Hut, standard huts with 6 bunks at $10. Across the region 23 huts carry a fee.

DOC bookings are needed at 5 huts, 5 are listed as within 3 hours of a road, and 4 take their water from a stream, which should be treated or boiled first. The region's 14 DOC campsites have a page of their own.
huts/fiordland: Fiordland National Park contains 53 of the region's 55 DOC huts, with one more in the Doubtful Sound/Patea area and one in the Southern fiords area. The huts hold 764 bunks in total, and a large share of them sit in the 7 Great Walk huts. Luxmore Hut has the most at 54, Iris Burn Hut and Lake Mackenzie Hut have 50 each, and Clinton Hut, Dumpling Hut, Mintaro Hut and Moturau Hut have 40 each.

Those Great Walk huts are also the region's 7 with flush toilets, and their rates are set by residency. Luxmore Hut lists $35 to $88 a night for NZ residents and $35 to $132 for international visitors. Clinton Hut, Dumpling Hut and Mintaro Hut list $30 to $106 for residents and $30 to $152 for international visitors, the top of Fiordland's $10 to $152 adult range. All told, 7 huts must be booked through DOC.

Away from the Great Walk huts, the picture changes. Standard huts are the largest group with 28, mostly 12-bunk huts at $10 for adults: Green Lake Hut, Hope Arm Hut, Kintail Hut, Loch Maree Hut and Supper Cove Hut are all listed that way. The 6 serviced huts include Lake Alabaster Hut with 26 bunks and Martins Bay Hut with 24, both at $10 to $25, and Port Craig School Hut with 20 bunks at $25.

There are 14 basic huts or bivvies and 14 free huts, against 41 that charge. 47 huts list heating and 50 list mattresses. A stream is the water supply at 12 huts, so plan to treat or boil it there. Just 4 huts are listed within 3 hours of a road. DOC's 13 campsites in Fiordland are covered separately.
huts/hawkes-bay: Hawke's Bay's DOC huts sit almost entirely in two forest parks: Kaweka Forest Park with 29 and Ruahine Forest Park with 25, out of 55 in the region. They are mostly small. The 55 huts share 328 bunks, and the categories are 33 standard huts, 19 basic huts or bivvies and just 3 serviced huts.

Many of the standard huts have 6 bunks and charge adults $10 a night. In Kaweka Forest Park that includes Cameron Hut, Harkness Hut, Makino Hut, Manson Hut and Middle Hill Hut; in Ruahine Forest Park, Dead Dog Hut and Kiritaki Hut. A step up in size, Daphne Hut and Triplex Hut in the Ruahine have 12 bunks each at the same $10 rate, as does Venison Tops Hut (Tira Lodge) in the Kaweka.

The 3 serviced huts include the two biggest. Te Puia Hut (Lodge) in Kaweka Forest Park has the most bunks with 26, at $25 for adults. Sunrise Hut in Ruahine Forest Park sleeps 20 and lists $25 to $30, the top of the region's $10 to $30 range, and Longview Hut has 12 bunks at $25. Only 2 huts must be booked through DOC, so nearly all are first come, first served.

Free huts number 17, against 36 with a fee. Awatere Hut and Dianes Hut in Ruahine Forest Park are free basic huts with 6 bunks each, both with heating and mattresses. Across all 55 huts, 40 have heating and 49 have mattresses. At 22 huts the water is from a stream, so carry a way to treat or boil it.
None of the huts here is listed as within 3 hours of a road. For tent nights, Hawke's Bay has 7 DOC campsites.
huts/manawatu-whanganui: The 43 DOC huts in Manawatū/Whanganui fall into two quite different groups. Ruahine Forest Park holds 33 of them, mostly standard huts at $10 a night. Whanganui National Park holds 7, among them the region's 2 Great Walk huts and 4 serviced huts. The Waitōtara Conservation Area has the other 3.

In the Ruahine, Waipawa Forks Hut has 12 bunks and Iron Gate Hut 10, while Barlow Hut, Cattle Creek Hut, Colenso Hut and Kelly Knight Hut have 8 each. Alice Nash Memorial Heritage Lodge is a standard hut with 8 bunks and lighting. Rangiwahia Hut is the park's serviced hut in the list, with 13 bunks at $25. Waikamaka Hut shows a fee but no rate.

Whanganui National Park has the two biggest huts. John Coull Hut has the most bunks in the region with 24, and Tīeke Marae/Kāinga has 20; both are Great Walk huts at $25 to $35 for adults, the top of the region's $10 to $35 range, and both list cooking facilities. The park's serviced huts, Pouri Hut with 12 bunks, Ngapurua Hut with 10, and Omaru Hut and Puketotara Hut with 8, all charge $25.

Across the region the 43 huts hold 308 bunks. The category count is 28 standard huts, 7 basic huts or bivvies, 6 serviced huts and 2 Great Walk huts. Only 6 huts are free and 36 carry a fee. Heating appears at 40 huts and mattresses at 42, so most have both. The 13 huts on stream water need it treated or boiled.
DOC bookings apply to 4 huts, 5 are listed as within 3 hours of a road, and 2 are marked closed in the data. DOC also runs 20 campsites in Manawatū/Whanganui.
huts/marlborough: Marlborough's 60 DOC huts are strikingly uniform. Every hut is either a standard hut (46) or a basic hut or bivvy (14); there are no serviced or Great Walk huts. Every listed adult rate is $10 a night. None of the huts must be booked through DOC, so they are all first come, first served.

The huts are small. Together they hold 335 bunks, and Rocks Hut in Mount Richmond Forest Park has the most at 16. Greigs Hut in the Leatham Conservation Area has 14, and Palmer Hut and Warden Hut in Ka Whata Tu o Rakihouia Clarence have 12 each. The rest sleep 10 or fewer.

Three areas tie for the most huts, with 16 each: Ka Whata Tu o Rakihouia Clarence, the Leatham Conservation Area and Mount Richmond Forest Park. In the Clarence, Snowgrass Hut and Forbes Hut (previously Seymour Hut) have 10 bunks each and Mt Fyffe Hut has 8. The Leatham huts include Barbers Hut, Bottom Gordon Hut, Bottom Misery Hut and Caves Hut, all standard huts with 6 bunks. In Mount Richmond Forest Park, Lake Chalice Hut, Lower Goulter Hut, Mid Goulter Hut and Richmond Saddle Hut have 8 bunks each.

Of the 60, 13 are free and 47 carry a fee. Mattresses are close to universal, listed at 59 huts, and heating appears at 47. Gosling Hut in the Glazebrook Conservation Area is the odd one among the listed huts: a basic hut with 6 bunks, heating and stream water but no mattresses listed, and a fee shown without a rate. Stream water is the supply at 35 huts in all, so treat or boil it.
Just 4 huts are listed within 3 hours of a road, a short list for a region of 60 huts. DOC also has 44 campsites across Marlborough, which have their own page.
huts/nelson-tasman: Nelson/Tasman has 99 DOC huts and 1,046 bunks, with two national parks holding most of them: Kahurangi National Park has 45 huts and Nelson Lakes National Park 24. Mount Richmond Forest Park adds 10. The mix is 50 standard huts, 25 basic huts or bivvies, 14 serviced huts and 10 Great Walk huts.

The listed Great Walk huts are in Abel Tasman National Park and Kahurangi National Park. Anchorage Hut and Bark Bay Hut in Abel Tasman National Park have 34 bunks each, the most in the region, and Awaroa Hut has 26. Their adult rates are $33 to $55 a night for NZ residents and $33 to $84 for international visitors, the top of the region's $10 to $84 range. In Kahurangi, Heaphy Hut has 32 bunks and James Mackay Hut and Perry Saddle Hut have 28, at $30 to $44 for residents and $30 to $66 for international visitors. All 7 huts with flush toilets are Great Walk huts.

Nelson Lakes National Park holds many of the serviced huts. Sabine Hut has 32 bunks, West Sabine Hut 30, Lakehead Hut 28, John Tait Hut 27 and Upper Travers Hut 24, all at $10 to $25 for adults. Angelus Hut has 28 bunks at $30. George Lyon Hut is a standard hut there with 16 bunks at $10.
Kahurangi has larger standard huts too. Kahurangi Keepers house sleeps 25, Karamea Bend Hut 22 and Kings Creek Hut 20, each at $10, and Salisbury Lodge is a serviced hut with 22 bunks at $25.

On fees, 25 huts are free and 73 charge, and 19 must be booked through DOC. Heating features at 86 huts and mattresses at 96, while 45 rely on stream water that needs treating or boiling. The data places 8 huts within 3 hours of a road and marks 1 as closed. DOC's 37 campsites in Nelson/Tasman are on a separate page.
huts/otago: Otago's 78 DOC huts are spread across many areas. The three with the most hold only 12, 12 and 9: Hāwea Conservation Park, Mount Aspiring National Park and Oteake Conservation Park. Basic huts and bivvies make up 34 of the total, standard huts 27, serviced huts 10, serviced alpine huts 5 and Great Walk huts 2, with 670 bunks between them.

Routeburn Falls Hut has the most bunks at 48. It and Routeburn Flats Hut, with 20, are the 2 Great Walk huts in Mount Aspiring National Park, listed at $30 to $88 a night for NZ residents and $30 to $132 for international visitors, the top of Otago's $10 to $132 adult range. In the same park, Dart Hut has 32 bunks at $10 to $25, and Shelter Rock Hut, Daleys Flat Hut and Young Hut are serviced huts at $25.

The serviced alpine huts are their own category. Aspiring Hut in the Matukituki Valley area has 32 bunks at $25 to $50, French Ridge Hut has 20 at $20 to $40, and Liverpool Hut has 10 at $35. Brewster Hut in the Makarora area has 12 bunks at $50. Of these, only Aspiring Hut lists heating.

Heating is listed at only 46 of the 78 huts, while mattresses appear at 67. In the Wānaka area, Fern Burn Hut, Highland Creek Hut and Roses Hut are standard huts with 12 bunks at $10, mattresses and untreated tap water, with no heating listed. Big Hut in the Rock and Pillar Conservation Area sleeps 16 at $12. In the Greenstone and Caples Conservation Areas, McKellar Hut, Mid Caples Hut and Greenstone Hut are serviced huts at $25 with flush toilets.

Fees apply at 46 huts and 26 are free, and 14 have to be booked through DOC. At 38 huts the water comes from a stream and should be treated or boiled before drinking. Just 5 Otago huts are listed within 3 hours of a road. The region also has 30 DOC campsites.
huts/southland: Southland's 70 DOC huts lean heavily towards the basic end: 50 are basic huts or bivvies, 18 are standard huts and 2 are Great Walk huts. With 453 bunks in total, most huts are small, and North Arm Hut has the most at 24.

Rakiura National Park holds 30 of the huts, more than any other area in the region. North Arm Hut and Port William Hut are its 2 Great Walk huts, with 24 bunks each and adult rates of $31 to $44 a night for NZ residents and $31 to $66 for international visitors, the top of the region's $10 to $66 range. The park's standard huts charge $10: Mason Bay Hut has 20 bunks, and Bungaree Hut, Freshwater Hut and Yankee River Hut have 16 each. Freshwater Hut is the region's one hut with flush toilets.

Rakiura also has a run of small hunters huts, among them North Pegasus Hunters Hut, South Pegasus Hunters Hut, Kellys Hunters Hut and Hapuatuna Hunters Hut, basic huts with 6 to 8 bunks that show a fee but no rate. A total of 21 huts in the region must be booked through DOC.

The Eyre Mountains/Taka Rā Haka Conservation Park has 16 huts and the Takitimu Conservation Area 12. In the Eyre Mountains, Mt Bee Bunkrooms is a free basic hut with 8 bunks and untreated tap water, and Cromel Base Hut is free with 6 bunks and stream water. In the Takitimu, Aparima Hut is a standard hut with 12 bunks at $10. Army Hut in the Snowdon Forest Conservation Area is free with 6 bunks.

Southland splits 27 free huts against 37 paid ones. Most huts list heating (57) and mattresses (63). Stream water supplies 27 huts; boil or treat it before drinking. Only 5 huts in the region appear in the data as within 3 hours of a road, and DOC campsites are few too, with 5 in Southland.
huts/wairarapa: Most of Wairarapa's 36 DOC huts are in Tararua Forest Park, which holds 23 of them. Aorangi Forest Park has 6 and the Holdsworth area 3. Standard huts make up 26 of the total, with 7 basic huts or bivvies and 3 serviced huts, and together they hold 349 bunks.

The Holdsworth area has only 3 huts but some of the biggest. Powell Hut has the most bunks in the region with 32, a serviced hut at $25 to $30 for adults, the top of the region's $10 to $30 range. Atiwhakatu Hut has 26 bunks at $10 to $15, and Jumbo Hut, also serviced, has 20 at $25. Powell Hut and Jumbo Hut both list cooking facilities.

In Tararua Forest Park, Totara Flats Hut is the serviced hut, with 26 bunks at $25. Alpha Hut and Tutuwai Hut have 20 bunks each at $10, Tarn Ridge Hut 16 and Mitre Flats Hut 14. Maungahuka Hut and Dundas Hut list mattresses and untreated tap water but no heating. Carkeek Hut, Dorset Ridge Hut, Neill Forks Hut and Nichols Hut are 6-bunk standard huts at $10. Cone Hut is a free basic hut with 6 bunks, heating and stream water.
Aorangi Forest Park's huts are small standard huts at $10: Sutherlands Hut has 7 bunks, and Kawakawa Hut, Mangatoetoe Hut and Pararaki Hut have 6 each.

Wairarapa's fee split is 29 paid huts to 6 free ones, and 4 huts must be booked through DOC. Heating shows up at 29 huts, mattresses at 32. Where water comes from a stream, at 11 huts, treat or boil it. The data puts 3 huts within 3 hours of a road. For camping rather than a bunk, DOC lists 6 campsites in Wairarapa.
huts/wellington-kapiti: Wellington/Kāpiti has 24 DOC huts with 243 bunks, in three main groups. Tararua Forest Park holds 15, the Catchpool Valley & Ōrongorongo Valley area 6, and the Ōtaki Forks area 3. The categories are 11 standard huts, 7 basic huts or bivvies and 6 serviced huts.

The 6 Ōrongorongo huts are the serviced ones, and 6 huts in the region must be booked through DOC. Turere Lodge has the most bunks with 32, Raukawa Lodge has 14, Haurangi Hut and Papatahi Hut 10, Jans Hut 9 and Boar Inn 4. Each shows a fee but no rate in the data, which is why the only adult rate listed for the region is $10. Raukawa Lodge is the region's one hut with flush toilets, and Turere Lodge, Haurangi Hut, Papatahi Hut and Jans Hut list cooking facilities.

That $10 rate applies at the standard huts. In the Ōtaki Forks area, Field Hut has 20 bunks, Parawai Lodge 18 and Waitewaewae Hut 16. In Tararua Forest Park, Te Matawai Hut and Waiopehu Hut have 18 bunks and Mangahao Flats Hut 16. South Ohau Hut has 10, and Kapakapanui Hut, Penn Creek Hut and Anderson Memorial Hut have 6 each.

The 7 free huts are all small. Burn Hut, Renata Hut, North Ohau Hut and Waiotauru Hut have 4 to 6 bunks, while Aokaparangi Hut, Dracophyllum Hut and North Mangahao Bivvy have just 2. Several of them have no heating listed, and Waiotauru Hut and North Mangahao Bivvy take their water from a stream.

Across all 24 huts, 17 list heating and 22 list mattresses. Stream water is the source at only 3 huts; treat or boil it there. The data places just 2 huts within 3 hours of a road, and DOC has 3 campsites in Wellington/Kāpiti.
huts/west-coast: The West Coast has 140 DOC huts with 885 bunks, and more than half of them are basic huts or bivvies: 74, against 51 standard huts, 8 serviced huts, 4 serviced alpine huts and 3 Great Walk huts. Free and paid huts are almost level, 68 free and 70 with a fee.

The areas with the most huts are river catchments rather than national parks. The Kokatahi River - Whitcombe River area has 29, the Kelly Range – Styx River area 19, and the Ahaura River and Lake Brunner catchments area 12. In the Kokatahi and Whitcombe, Cedar Flat Hut and Frew Hut are standard huts with 12 and 10 bunks at $10. Dillon Hut and Grassy Flat Hut in the Kelly Range area have 10 bunks each at the same rate.

Welcome Flat Hut in Westland Tai Poutini National Park has the most bunks at 31, a serviced hut that shows a fee without a rate. The same park holds serviced alpine huts: Centennial Hut with 20 bunks and Pioneer Hut with 12, both with a fee, and Chancellor Hut with 12 at $25. Almer Hut in the Franz Josef Glacier/Kā Roimata o Hine Hukatere area is another, 12 bunks at $25.

The 3 Great Walk huts are in Paparoa National Park. Moonlight Tops Hut lists $50 to $78 a night for NZ residents and $50 to $117 for international visitors, the top of the region's $10 to $117 range. Pororari Hut lists $50 to $61 for residents, and Ces Clark Hut $50 for residents. In the Lewis Pass Scenic Reserve, Cannibal Gorge Hut and Kōhanga Atawhai – Manson Nicholls Hut have 20 bunks each at $10 to $25.

Nearly every hut lists mattresses, 135 of the 140, while heating appears at 94. With 71 huts drawing water from a stream, a way to treat or boil it belongs in the pack. DOC bookings are needed at 11 huts. The data lists 15 huts within 3 hours of a road, and the region also has 14 DOC campsites.
